reviews.comment: Took this class online over the summer. His lectures were on the boring side and his voice is very monotone, though there were a decent number of good examples. The material is hard and grading is very exam-heavy, over half of the grade, but alleviated a bit by the fact that there's bonus points available on every exam.

He has made this class unquestionably harder compared to other professors. All the people that I have known to do well in his class rarely showed up to class. If you feel that you have a really good grasp on statistics, take his class. If not, take anyone else.

Dr. Horn does care a lot and will try to help you, but when it comes to the actual class.... He kind of just assumes that you'll be able to solve the type of problem that he can, even though he's been doing this for like at least ten years. It's been brought up in class that the exams, which are worth a lot, are too difficult, but nothing changes.

The grading criteria in this class is wack (not Dr. Horn's fault; it's the department). However, Dr. Horn told us clearly what to expect and how to receive a good grade in the class. If you put in a little effort, you will get a good grade. Everyone complaining here is mad that a writing intensive course had a lot of writing... Overall, great prof.

Dr. Horn is one of the better professors in the department. He is very understanding of things going on in other classes and often extends deadlines for the entire class. He gets a bad rep because some people don't know how to follow instructions on assignments, but overall is an easy grader. Only bad thing was that he took a long time to grade.

There are only two ways most people come out of this class: Extremely resentful (because he's not that great of a prof, but hey he tries), or extremely delusional that he "wasn't THAT bad" (to be fair, he wasn't THAT bad but still). Most the difficulty comes from him being totally out of touch with his students. 

7/10 overall, because he does TRY.

This class is an absolute waste of time and has no reason to be a 3-credit-hour course. The grading was weird, with no numerical values but simply "does not meet expectations," "meets expectations," and "exceeds expectations. The class is a writing intensive course, and if you fail the writing portion, you fail the whole class.

For Biomedical Engineering 201, this class is horrible. The prof never responds to any emails. A ton of work. Would not recommend this class to my worst enemy. The assignments are all useless and a waste of time too. I spend more time working on this class than any other class and I am taking 19 hours. Make it make sense. Worst class I have taken.
reviews.ratingTags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: BMEN 201 - This class is so much work it is insane. I think I spend the most amount of time per week on this class. Grading takes forever to come back, emails are never answered, classes are soo boring. I know this class is mandatory, but genuinely one of my least favorite classes ever. Almost every class we have like 4 more assignments.

Dr. Horn is great! His lectures provide everything you need to succeed in this course, and he is very accessible if you need his help on anything. The homework can be challenging, but it serves as excellent exam prep if you make sure to take the time conceptually understand each problem. Biotransport is a very cool course if you apply yourself.
Dr. Horn talks like a sweet angel from heaven. His lectures are good. Start early on homework. This class requires some good coding skills if you want to get the 100pt extra credits.

Dr. Horn really does care about his students. He gave a lot of extra credit, as well as clear instructions about what you need to know/study. Each test has about one really hard question, but he is very generous with partial credit. He makes himself available to his students and cares about feedback for improving! I learned a lot from his class!
